applicable_when: The kernel copies from a contiguous (1960,160) input to a strided (10,160,14,14) output with stride (100352,1,7168,512). The current flat 1D tiling with XBLOCK=128 mixes x0 (column, 0..159) and x1 (row, 0..1959) indices within each block. The output store address is x0 + 512*x1, meaning consecutive xindex values write to addresses 512 floats (2KB) apart — completely non-coalesced. This causes every store to touch a separate cache line, explaining the 0% L1 hit rate and high L1TEX scoreboard stall (55% of cycles). Two prior autotune attempts (item_ids 1e1a29e4, 7578f7ea) failed correctness because they changed XBLOCK without fixing the index decomposition. The correct fix is to restructure the kernel with a 2D tile: YBLOCK rows x ROW_WIDTH=160 columns, so that within each block all 160 output writes in a row are contiguous (stride-1 in x0 dimension). This makes output stores fully coalesced. Simultaneously, increasing the number of rows per block (YBLOCK) increases in-flight memory requests to hide the 23.1-cycle L1TEX latency and reduces the grid from 2450 to ceil(1960/YBLOCK) blocks, eliminating the partial-wave tail.
